summary: Two copies of railroad still can't work together: the load-time error says so, but the UI stays inert
detail: 0.12's guard (signals.ts, 'One copy per page') logs an error naming both copies; it does not make them cooperate. The whole fix, only as one change: keep the tracking state (currentListener, currentDeps, batchDepth, activeFlush, pendingEffects, the dispose stack, the provider registry) on globalThis[Symbol.for('@blueshed/railroad@1')], and recognise a signal by that brand instead of `instanceof Signal`. A brand alone is worse than nothing: `{doc.data}` goes from a visible '[object Object]' to a silently stale value and when() still never switches, because .get() registers with its own copy's listener. Repro: link delta by `file:` so it brings its own node_modules/@blueshed/railroad, render `{doc.data}` and a when() on it. Until then the skill's 'Local development across repos' (pack tarballs, one copy) stands.

summary: A value change inside the same truthiness, or the same route pattern, doesn't re-render: when() and destructured params
detail: when(sig, fn) rebuilds only when truthiness flips, so /sites/42 → /sites/99 keeps showing site 42; a route handler that destructures ({ id }) runs once per pattern and keeps the first id. Both are documented now (skill §9, routes.ts header), not fixed. API options: when(cond, (v$) => …) passing a narrowed ReadonlySignal<NonNullable<T>> to the branch (also removes delta users' `!`); for routes, re-run a handler that doesn't take params$ (handler.length < 2) on a param change, or a `keyed` option like Solid's <Show keyed>. Breaking either way; decide before 1.0.

summary: Glitch-free only while computeds read the same signals every run: a computed that switches its reads can be seen half-updated
detail: Topological order is fixed at subscription depth; a computed like `flag.get() ? b.get() : a.get()` can deepen after its readers were ordered, so on a later write one reader may run once on half-updated values before it re-runs on the settled ones (every write still settles). The claim is narrowed in the signals.ts header, README, skill and CLAUDE.md. The real fix is push-dirty / pull-recompute (the colouring model of Preact signals, Vue 3.4, Reactively): a computed re-checks its sources when read. A randomized checker found 0 glitches on fixed graphs over ~107k runs and ~600 per 300 dynamic graphs; a 4-line partial ('notify readers when a computed deepens') left ~60 and added redundant runs, so it was not taken. Commit the checker with the fix.

summary: Importing the root barrel declares a global JSX namespace, which clashes with React's in a mixed app
detail: `import … from '@blueshed/railroad'` pulls jsx.ts's `declare global { namespace JSX }`; a React app that also imports delta's client (which imports the barrel) gets TS2300 Duplicate identifier 'Element'. Subpath imports are clean. Fix (breaking for `jsx: react` users): move the global declaration to an opt-in `@blueshed/railroad/jsx-global` import; jsx-runtime.ts already covers `jsx: react-jsx`. delta's half (import subpaths) is in delta's todo.jsonl.

summary: A function child that returns a Node renders it as text, with a warning
detail: `{() => cond.get() ? <A/> : <B/>}` warns and renders '[object HTMLDivElement]'. Either make a function child returning a Node a real dynamic region (bracket comments, dispose the old subtree, as when() does), or keep when()/list() as the only way and make the warning the documented answer. Decide with the when(cond, v$) item.

summary: RouteHandler still admits Promise<Node>, whose post-await bindings leak; navigate() sets the hash a tick late
detail: Kept for back-compat and documented: a bare Promise<Node> renders, but what it builds after its first await has no owner scope and outlives the route; the thunk form is the supported one. Deprecate then drop Promise<Node> from the type. navigate() is async by way of hashchange, so route() read straight after navigate() shows the old path; set the hash signal synchronously in navigate().

summary: No shared blueshed plugin or router skill tells an agent which of eta, delta and railroad to use, and delta-doc's own description captures every 'live multi-user app' request before railroad or eta are considered
detail: architect.md §5: delta-doc's SKILL.md claims every "live multi-user app" request and never mentions eta or railroad by name as an alternative. Proposed shape (architect §6.2, proposal-final §5): one `blueshed` plugin in a marketplace repo holding a router skill under about 800 words (the decision guide), WIRE.md, one sandbox hook, one release command and MCP wiring; package skills stay inside the npm packages, synced at session start, restricted to @blueshed/* plus an allowlist. Namespacing under `blueshed:` ends skill/command shadowing in multi-repo sessions (architect F2: in a session with eta, delta and railroad all open, invoking "railroad" loaded delta's committed, hand-synced copy instead of railroad's own -- now largely moot since delta re-syncs from npm at each release) and retires railroad's own /publish once `release` lands. Same item in eta's and delta's todo.jsonl.

summary: railroad, delta and eta each run their own /publish command with different gates, changelog headings, commit formats and tag styles instead of one namespaced release flow
detail: architect.md F8: railroad's /publish gates on `bun test --coverage && bun run check`, but its CI (publish.yml) also runs the WebView suite and check:consumer, so a release can pass /publish locally and fail CI; delta's gates on `bun run ci` (Docker, which its own CLAUDE.md says not to run in the sandbox); changelog headings differ (`## 0.11.0` here vs `## [0.5.1] -- date` in delta vs eta's `## [0.46.0] - date`), and commit-message format, annotated-vs-light tag and Bun-pinning-in-CI all differ too. proposal-final §5: one `commands/release.md` under the blueshed plugin, namespaced so it stops shadowing, calling each repo's own sandbox-safe `bun run release:gate`. Same item in eta's todo.jsonl; delta's own version of this problem is its todo #12.
